text:
Maria G.: Heads-up — prod Mistral FP8 canary is showing a ~12% tail-latency regression after last night's kernel-selector tweak. Observed p95/p99 shifts over 24h: baseline p95 85ms p99 210ms -> canary p95 95ms p99 235ms. Not a huge throughput drop but tail impact is concerning. Anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:

Samir: I saw something similar when we swapped the attention kernel ordering. Quick check: the selector moved attn_opt_v2 ahead of attn_opt_v1_int8_fallback for short sequences, which improved avg latency but increased worst-case for some kv-heavy traces. Can you paste the workload profile?

Maria G.: Here are two reproducer runs from the canary host (seq=512, batch=8):

```
$ python perf/bench.py --model mistral-xl --quant fp8 --kernel-selector=canary --batch 8 --seq 512 --warm 50 --iters 200
avg latency: 78.4 ms
p95: 94.7 ms
p99: 236.1 ms
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.84
cpu_context_switches: +18%
```

Baseline (before selector change):
```
avg latency: 80.9 ms
p95: 85.0 ms
p99: 210.2 ms
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.90
cpu_context_switches: baseline
```

Lex: Two quick hypotheses: 1) kernel attn_opt_v2 increases per-request memory working set, causing higher KV cache pressure/evictions on hosts with many concurrent sessions; 2) the batching heuristic now favors packing slightly larger batches which amplifies worst-case latency when a large prefix misses cache. Did the canary tweak change max_batch or batching window?

Maria G.: We didn't touch batching config, only selector ordering. But perf-bot early warning did show a rise in page-faults and context switches on the affected hosts.

perf-bot: alert: host-ml-23 p99 latency spike detected, correlates with kernel_selector=canary, spike_start=2026-11-02T03:12Z

Samir: OK let's bisect. Steps I'd run locally: 1) repro microbench with per-kernel timings: --profile-kernel and --kv-trace, 2) run with kv_lazy_eviction toggled, 3) compare attn_opt_v2 vs attn_opt_v1_int8_fallback, 4) run same on Qwen/Llama to see if model-specific wiring changes sensitivity.

Andrew (eng-ml): I already ran per-kernel profile on mistral-x: attaching snippet (trimmed):
```
kernel_times:
  attn_opt_v2: mean 1.8ms, std 0.9ms, 99th 6.6ms
  attn_opt_v1_int8_fallback: mean 2.1ms, std 0.6ms, 99th 3.2ms
io / kvcopy:
  kvcopy spikes correlate with attn_opt_v2 p99
```

Lex: That explains it: attn_opt_v2 has lower median but heavier tail due to occasional large KV copy operations. If selector favored it, we reduced median but exposed those KV spikes at tail.

Maria G.: Thoughts on mitigation? Options I see: revert selector ordering, add a tail-aware penalty in kernel score, or tweak KV caching packing (align pages) to reduce kvcopy cost.

Samir: Prefer adding a tail-aware penalty short-term and roll out a canary that de-prioritizes attn_opt_v2 for requests with kv-depth > X. Patch suggestion (quick):
```
kernel_priority_score(kernel, ctx) = base_score - alpha*kv_depth - beta*recent_p99(kernel)
# with alpha=0.6 for now
```

Andrew (eng-ml): Also propose a small KV change we tested in staging: kv_lazy_eviction=false reduced p99 by ~18% for the same reproducer (fewer eviction-induced copies). Might be less risky than touching kernel selector globally.

Lex: We should collect model-specific sensitivity. For Qwen the large heads/long seq behavior may behave differently; for Llama FP8 we saw earlier that packing alignment reduces misaligned loads and helps tail. Let's run a 4-way matrix: {Mistral,Qwen,Llama} x {attn_opt_v2, attn_opt_v1_int8_fallback} x {kv_lazy_eviction true/false} with the same seq/batch and compare p99 and kvcopy counts. I'll sketch a small jobflow.

Maria G.: Agree. I'll spin up the matrix on prod-like hosts and post results in this thread. Short-term action: revert the selector change on the canary cluster and pin it until we have matrix results. Who wants the revert?

Samir: I can push the revert and open a PR for the tail-aware scoring. Will run the matrix after revert completes.

perf-bot: deploy note: revert applied to canary-rls at 2026-11-02T04:05Z, owner=Samir

Maria G.: Nice. For sharing configs, here's the minimal quant/kernel profile we should add to the model-catalog for Mistral (put in config repo under inference/profiles/mistral_fp8_tailaware.json):

```json
{
  "model": "mistral-xl",
  "quant_profile": "fp8",
  "kernel_priority": ["attn_opt_v1_int8_fallback","attn_opt_v2","matmul_fast"],
  "batching": {"max_batch": 24, "window_ms": 8},
  "kv_config": {"kv_lazy_eviction": false, "kv_page_align": true},
  "notes": "tail-aware ordering; avoid attn_opt_v2 for kv_depth>8"
}
```

Andrew (eng-ml): Please include perf numbers and the experiment link in the repo commit so oncall can roll back safely. Also add a reproducible perf test id.

Maria G.: Will add results. Lex will run the Qwen/Llama runs and post here. Expected next steps: Samir reverts + PR, Lex cross-model matrix, commit profile with test artifacts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Lex: Quick FYI — initial Qwen run (seq512,b8) shows attn_opt_v2 p99 also higher but kv_hit_rate unaffected (Qwen's kv layout handles the copies better). So model-specific profiles make sense.

Maria G.: Good context. Leaving this thread open for results; will update with the matrix output and commit link.
